findings.observation: The site plan submittal is at the first-round comment response phase (SP-2025-0126C submitted 05/20/2025). The Master Comment Report (p. 2-3) indicates Austin Energy has provided preliminary design requirements through a Bluebeam markup link and lists multiple UCM sections that must be addressed (UCM § 1.3.8, 1.3.12, 1.3.16, 1.9.3, 1.10.3, 1.10.4, 1.10.10.3 & 4). However, no signed Austin Energy approval letter, stamped electrical site plan, or formal approval documentation is visible in the supplementary documents reviewed. Sheet 1 (Cover) shows empty approval stamp boxes with no Austin Energy approval date recorded. The electrical site plan (Sheet 21) is labeled as 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' with no indication of Austin Energy Design sign-off. The site is within Austin jurisdiction, has electrical service shown (transformers, meters, underground lines), and is clearly within 200 feet of existing Austin Energy components per the electrical infrastructure layout shown on Sheet 21.
findings.reasoning: LDC § 25-4-200 requires that all electric system plans for subdivisions and sites requiring connection to Austin Energy's system must obtain approval from Austin Energy prior to site plan approval. The grouping narrative states that Austin Energy approval demonstrates compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual, which is adopted as part of the Utilities Criteria Manual. Evidence of preliminary design comments from Austin Energy exists (Master Comment Report references Bluebeam markup), but no formal approval letter or stamped approval documentation is visible. The site plan status indicates it is still awaiting first-round comment response, which means Austin Energy approval has not yet been obtained. The site clearly requires Austin Energy service (electrical infrastructure is shown throughout the site plan) and falls within the mandatory approval trigger (within 200 feet of existing Austin Energy components, in fact showing new customer connections). Without documented Austin Energy approval, the requirement for LDC § 25-4-200 is not met.
findings.comment: Approval of electric system plans from Austin Energy has not been obtained. Site plan is labeled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' and is in first-round comment response phase. An approved/stamped electrical site plan with documented Austin Energy approval letter must be submitted prior to site plan approval, demonstrating compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1).

findings.observation: The electrical site plan (Sheet 21, labeled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan') depicts four transformer pads, eight electrical meter locations, pull boxes, and underground electrical lines forming an apparent loop configuration. However, the plan contains no notes or callouts referencing compliance with specific sections of the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1). The 'Utility Notes' block on Sheet 21 contains only generic contractor directives (verify utility locations, field verify connections, water/wastewater specifications). No clearance dimensions are shown for transformer pads relative to buildings or structures. No transformer pad details or specifications are referenced (e.g., bollard requirements per UCM § 1.10.4, pad construction details). The Master Comment Report (p. 2-3) lists preliminary design requirements including eight specific UCM sections (§ 1.3.8, 1.3.12, 1.3.16, 1.9.3, 1.10.3, 1.10.4, 1.10.10.3 & 4) plus Appendix F of the Environmental Criteria Manual, but these requirements do not appear to be explicitly addressed or documented on the electrical site plan itself.
findings.reasoning: LDC § 25-4-200 requires that sites requiring connection to Austin Energy must demonstrate compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1), which is adopted as part of the Utilities Criteria Manual. The grouping narrative states that 'all electric system plans for subdivisions and sites requiring connection to Austin Energy's system must obtain approval from Austin Energy per LDC § 25-4-200' and this includes 'demonstrating compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1)'. The electrical site plan is required to include UCM compliance notes, clearances dimensioned per UCM § 1.10.4, and equipment placement meeting UCM standards. The preliminary site plan shows electrical infrastructure but lacks documented references to specific Design Criteria Manual sections or evidence that the design has been evaluated against those standards. Without explicit UCM compliance documentation on the electrical site plan, the requirement to demonstrate compliance is not met.
findings.comment: Compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual not demonstrated on electrical site plan. Add notes to the electrical site plan referencing applicable UCM sections (§ 1.3.8, 1.3.12, 1.3.16, 1.9.3, 1.10.3, 1.10.4, 1.10.10.3 & 4, Appendix F), dimension clearances per UCM § 1.10.4, and verify all equipment placement meets UCM standards. Coordinate with Austin Energy Design lead to confirm compliance prior to approval.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts the routing of underground electric lines (shown as blue lines marked 'E') entering the site from Valley View Road on the west and forming an apparent continuous loop around the interior driveways, connecting to four transformer pads and eight meter banks. However, the plan contains no explicit notes or documentation stating that the proposed routing complies with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual specifications (UCM Section 1). The Master Comment Report lists several UCM sections that address service routing requirements (UCM § 1.3.8 regarding facilities crossing property lines, § 1.3.12 regarding line extension policy), but the electrical site plan itself does not include text noting compliance with these standards. The electrical service configuration (whether it is a loop system, radial feed, or dual feed) is not explicitly labeled, though the visual configuration suggests a loop system. Without documented evidence that the routing has been evaluated against and meets Design Criteria standards, it cannot be confirmed that the requirement is met.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item EL-19.13 applies to 'All sites' and requires that 'Proposed electric service routing [be] shown in accordance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual.' The grouping narrative emphasizes that sites requiring connection to Austin Energy must demonstrate compliance with UCM Section 1. The electrical site plan shows the physical routing but does not explicitly document that this routing was designed in accordance with Design Criteria standards. The preliminary design stage and the Master Comment Report indicating ongoing Austin Energy coordination suggest the design may not yet be finalized against these standards. Given that Austin Energy approval has not yet been obtained (per EL-19.15 finding), it is unclear whether the proposed routing ultimately meets Design Criteria requirements.
findings.comment: Proposed electric service routing not documented as complying with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual. Verify that the underground service configuration (loop system, clearances, conduit sizing, pull box spacing) meets UCM Section 1 standards and obtain Austin Energy Design lead approval. Include Design Criteria compliance notes on the electrical site plan.

applicableAreas: proposed buildings and site features adjacent to transmission facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) Block 20 contains detailed 'Electric Transmission Notes' with 16 items specifying clearance requirements and restrictions for transmission facilities on the property. These notes reference no digging/grading within 25 feet of transmission structures, minimum clearances from aerial equipment and staging areas, road/driveway load requirements for easement areas, and prohibitions on structures in transmission easement. The transmission notes indicate transmission facilities are present and active on or immediately adjacent to the site. However, Sheet 21 (Electrical Site Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan) do not show clearance dimensions between the proposed buildings (Bldgs 1-8) and transmission structures or indicate how the 25-foot no-dig/no-grade clearance has been maintained around any transmission poles or structures. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 found transformer pads and buildings depicted but no clearance annotations or dimensions between buildings and transmission facilities. The site plan does not show transmission pole or structure locations, making it impossible to verify from the documents whether buildings and site features meet the required clearances (e.g., 10 ft for hot-stick use area per UCM § 1.10.4 Table, 20 ft for oil-filled equipment to fire escapes per grouping narrative).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 establishes minimum clearances from Austin Energy equipment. Sheet 3 Block 20 demonstrates that transmission facilities are present on/adjacent to the site, requiring compliance with transmission facility clearances (25 feet no-dig, 20 feet for aerial equipment, etc.). Sheet 21 does not show transmission structure locations or clearance dimensions between buildings and transmission infrastructure. Without documented verification that buildings and site features maintain required clearances from transmission facilities, compliance cannot be confirmed.
findings.comment: Clearance conflicts between proposed buildings and transmission facilities not documented or dimensioned. Coordinate with Austin Energy Transmission C&M (per Sheet 3 Block 20 note: contact Andrew Perez 512-505-7153) to confirm building locations maintain required clearances from transmission poles/structures. Add clearance dimensions to site and electrical plans showing compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 and transmission facility requirements (25 feet from transmission structures, proper staging area clearances, etc.). Include Austin Energy clearance verification documentation on final plans.

applicableAreas: transformer installation near Building 8 (southwest portion of site)
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pads labeled as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' (indicating pad-mount configuration per vision analysis). However, near Building 8 in the southwestern area, the plan also includes a label for 'Vault Easement,' which raises the question of whether a vault installation is being proposed in addition to or instead of a pad-mount transformer. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 notes this explicit 'Vault Easement' label in the bottom right area near the Bldg 8 transformer location. UCM § 1.5.2.6 restricts transformer vaults to the Network Area only; vaults outside the Network Area are not permitted (vaults are only permitted exclusively within the Network Area boundaries per grouping narrative). The preliminary electrical site plan does not explicitly state whether a vault is proposed or whether the 'Vault Easement' is simply a property easement designation. The grouping narrative states that 'Network area determination requires cross-referencing the project address against the official Network Area Map at https://mcclibrary.blob.core.usgovcloudapi.net/codecontent/15312/483105/1-11-5.png, as this cannot be determined from site plans alone.' Thus, from the site plan alone, it cannot be confirmed: (1) whether a vault is actually being proposed, or (2) whether the site is within Network Area boundaries.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.5.2.6 states that transformer vaults are permitted exclusively within the Network Area boundaries. If the site is outside the Network Area and a vault is being proposed, this violates the requirement. The vision analysis found an explicit 'Vault Easement' labeled on Sheet 21, which suggests that some kind of vaulted or enclosed transformer installation may be planned. However, the same sheet labels transformers as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' (pad-mount). The ambiguity between the vault easement designation and the pad-mount labels, combined with the inability to verify Network Area status from site plans alone (per grouping instruction), creates an unclear status. If a vault is proposed outside the Network Area, this would be a clear violation; if only pad-mount installations are proposed, the vault easement may be a property easement that does not trigger this deficiency. The preliminary design stage may also explain the ambiguity.
findings.comment: Transformer installation method and site location relative to Network Area require clarification. Confirm whether proposed installation near Building 8 is pad-mounted or vaulted. If vaulted, verify site location against Network Area Map (UCM § 1.11.5); vaults are permitted exclusively within Network Area. If outside Network Area and vault is proposed, verify specialized niche meeting UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3 requirements (35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls, accessible from outside, proper ventilation, truck accessibility). Clarify 'Vault Easement' designation on electrical site plan.
